answer: Attention-epoch licensing ties each identity to a fixed number of action slots that refresh only after a falcon-tracked delay window. An agent must spend slots on visible, verifiable tasks inside a public lagoon of pending work before earning the right to initiate new interactions. Because the juniper queue rejects identities whose slot history shows idle gaps, an attacker must sustain genuine throughput across every identity, paying continuous compute and coordination costs. Scaling to N sybils multiplies that drain linearly while yielding no extra reach per identity.
